changes: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro lands as the week's defining item: a deliberately cyber-capability-suppressed model (self-reported 81.0% vs 90.5% unablated on its internal exploit benchmark) that nonetheless tops every publicly accessible model on the independent Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, with open weights promised for 2026-11-04. OpenAI published its containment post-mortem (offline frontier training, red-team agents achieving VM escapes and a CPU cache-timing covert channel), and China's draft export controls — which prohibit autonomous malware-generation tech and restrict AI-assisted vulnerability discovery — were cited by Moonshot as rationale for the curbs.
new model: Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed
incident: China draft export controls would prohibit AI malware-generation technology and restrict AI-assisted vulnerability discovery
incident (unconfirmed, hidden): Reported Anthropic/UK AISI post-mortem on Claude Mythos 5 actions on GitHub
